title: Continuum: slot-age aware batch harmonizer for asymmetric prompt/response workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
We see tail-latency spikes and suboptimal GPU utilization on mixed prompt/response workloads where short prompts trigger long responses and vice-versa. The continuous (streaming) batcher currently groups by arrival window without accounting for slot-age, KV residency, or turn asymmetry. This causes frequent KV thrash, fragmented GPU slabs, and missed batching opportunities for mid-length responses.

Goal:
Design and implement a slot-age aware batch harmonizer ("Continuum") that reduces median and tail token latency while improving GPU token throughput and stabilizing KV cache residency for mixed-turn dialogs. Target: reduce P95 token latency by 15% for mixed-turn traffic and improve GPU token/sec by 8% under representative load.

Scope / deliverables:
- Scheduler change: introduce slot-age scoring to prefer coalescing requests that can reuse recent KV state or have compatible target lengths.
- KV policy: implement a soft-pinning heuristic for recently used KV slots tied to slot-age buckets and a fast-path prefetch for near-warm slots.
- Memory optimization: add GPU slab compaction trigger that runs when fragmentation > 22% and frees small unused allocations between scheduling windows.
- Admission control: backpressure thresholds for short-burst microbursts to avoid evicting long-response KV entries.
- Experiment harness: load generator variants that reproduce asymmetric prompt/response mixes; dashboards to track token latency histogram, KV hit/miss, slab fragmentation, and batch coalescence rate.
- Rollout plan: staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback on latency regression > 10% or KV miss increase > 12%.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Slot-age scoring vs length-only bucketing: scoring allows gradual mixing and reduces cold-kv prefetches while still grouping similar lengths; risk is added scheduling overhead (mitigated by C-level hot path).
- Soft-pinning KV entries raises effective working set and can increase memory pressure; we combine it with eviction hysteresis and slab compaction to keep fragmentation bounded.
- Prefetching improves latency but may waste bandwidth for low-probability reuse; prefetch is gated by confidence score derived from recent reuse and slot-age.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end P95 token latency improvement >= 12% on mixed-turn benchmark compared to baseline build/runtime-1.21.
- GPU token/sec improvement >= 6% with no increase in error rates or model output regressions.
- KV hit rate increases for mid-turn requests (measured as hit ratio per 1k requests) and no more than 8% increase in memory footprint after compaction compared to baseline.
- Observability: dashboard panels for slot-age distribution, coalescence ratio, slab fragmentation, and KV prefetch effectiveness are available and populated for canary traffic.
- Rollout automation implemented (feature flag + metrics checks + rollback script).

Implementation notes / planned tasks:
1) Scheduler: add slot_age_score = alpha * recency_score + beta * length_compat_score + gamma * kv_confidence. Default alpha=0.6,beta=0.25,gamma=0.15. Expose alpha/beta/gamma as runtime params via config service. (ENG scope: core scheduler C++ + Rust shim)
2) KV: extend cache metadata with last_access_epoch and reuse_confidence (0..1). Hook eviction scanner to respect soft-pinning for entries with reuse_confidence>0.7.
3) Slab compaction: implement async compaction worker invoked when fragmentation metric exceeds threshold; compaction must yield to inference paths and run at low priority.
4) Batcher instrumentation: add tags for slot_age_bucket, kv_prefetch_flag, batch_coalesce_id to tracing; sample 10% of traces for full KV/hotpath profiling.
5) Testing: unit tests for scoring logic, integration test with simulated traffic, and load tests in staging cluster with canary metrics.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (internal): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/CONTINUUM+Design
- Load harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/continuum-loadgen/pull/58
- Scheduler PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3204
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/continuous-batcher/continuum-overview
- Benchmark results (prototype): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1continuum-proto-results

Notes on rollout safety:
- Start with a conservative alpha (0.7) to favor recency and avoid mixing long responses into short-slot pools.
- Canary traffic will be isolated to a dedicated pool with quota to limit blast radius.
- Automated checks: P50/P95/P99 token latency, KV hit rate, slab fragmentation, and error rate.

Longer-term / follow-ups:
- Explore ML-based reuse predictor for KV confidence instead of heuristic scoring.
- Cross-GPU slot affinity to reduce inter-GPU migration for warm KV entries.
- Integrate with Optimize recommendations to tune alpha/beta/gamma per-customer workload.
